SMTO-ART-0026 — A Task result was too large for SMTO to save

GUID: e2c1f523-7595-4834-8ca4-c7ee6b5f1ebf
Slug: artifact-inline-limit
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • One step in this Task produced a result larger than 16 MB, so SMTO couldn't save it with the conversation. Anything that step already did isn't undone; only its result couldn't be kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reply in the conversation asking SMTO to write the large output to a file and show you a short summary instead of the full text. Files are kept under Artifacts from this run, which can hold far more than a single step's result.
  2. Before asking SMTO to repeat the step, check on the computer it ran on whether its work already happened, such as a file being written or a setting changed. Only saving the result failed; the step itself may already have run, and repeating it could do the work twice.
  3. If you only need part of the output, ask for just that part, for example the first 1,000 lines or only the lines with errors. A smaller result fits under the 16 MB limit and is saved normally.

What success looks like

  • The output appears as a file under Artifacts from this run, and the step shows a short summary instead of an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the conversation or its history to make room; that removes saved work and doesn't raise the limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • RunStore.put refused to store an operation result because its UTF-8 serialized size exceeds the native run store's fixed 16 MiB per-result limit.

What this means

  • Inline receipt/artifact publication serializes the payload and finds its UTF-8 representation above 16 MiB. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Inline receipt/artifact publication serializes the payload and finds its UTF-8 representation above 16 MiB.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect encoded payload size and any existing complete file deliverable.

How to fix it

  • The 16 MiB check in RunStore.put (src/agent_runtime/current_run/native_store.py) is fixed; have the operation write its output as a file artifact in the run's artifact directory and return a short summary instead of embedding the whole value. Do not delete existing receipts or conversation history to work around the size check, and do not re-run completed operations only to re-publish their output.
  • Use an existing file deliverable through the supported artifact publication path instead of embedding the entire value. Do not discard or regenerate completed work solely to publish it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact output is published through a supported file artifact without regenerating completed work.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
